Uncover briefly to thicken the sauce.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Creamy Mushroom Potato Stew
tagline: Potatoes and mushrooms simmer with leeks, thyme, and a modest splash of cream.
steps: Brown mushrooms in olive oil and set aside; allow 5–7 minutes over medium-high heat so the surfaces color instead of steaming.
Soften leeks and garlic; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Add potato cubes and thyme.
Add water to cover halfway and simmer until potatoes are tender; keep a gentle bubble for about 15–20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Return mushrooms, stir in cream and black pepper.
Reduce for 3 minutes.

title: Eggplant Tomato Stew
tagline: Silky eggplant, tomatoes, peppers, and paprika cook into a rich meat-free pot.
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Brown eggplant cubes in olive oil in batches; cook for 4–6 minutes over medium-high heat, leaving each side undisturbed long enough to color.
Soften onion, pepper, and garlic and add paprika; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Add tomatoes and cook until saucy; allow 6–8 minutes over medium heat, stirring until the raw smell is gone and the mixture looks glossy.
Return eggplant, cover, and simmer until silky but not collapsed; keep a gentle bubble for about 8–12 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Courgette Chickpea Skillet
tagline: Courgette and chickpeas get crisp edges with lemon, garlic, and herbs.
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Brown courgette half-moons in olive oil without crowding; cook for 4–6 minutes over medium-high heat, leaving each side undisturbed long enough to color.
Add onion and garlic and cook until fragrant.
Fold in chickpeas and mixed herbs and let the edges color; 1–2 minutes is enough for the greens to soften while keeping their color.
Finish with lemon and black pepper.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Maize Sukuma Skillet
tagline: Fresh maize kernels and sukuma cook with tomato, onion, and paprika.
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Slice the kernels from the maize cobs.
Soften onion in oil, add paprika and tomatoes, and cook until saucy; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Add maize kernels with a splash of water and cover until tender.
Fold in sliced sukuma and cook for 5 minutes.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Tomato Cabbage Egg Skillet
tagline: Cabbage and tomato soften beneath eggs for a fast, inexpensive dinner.
steps: Prepare all vegetables and garnishes first; crack the eggs into a clean bowl unless the method calls for cooking them whole.
Soften onion and shredded cabbage in oil; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Add paprika and tomatoes and cook until the mixture is nearly dry; allow 6–8 minutes over medium heat, stirring until the raw smell is gone and the mixture looks glossy.
Make six wells and crack in the eggs.
Cover until the whites set and serve from the skillet.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Savory Tomato Oats
tagline: Creamy oats take on tomato, spinach, spring onion, and black pepper.
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Soften diced tomato in olive oil until saucy; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Add oats and water and simmer, stirring, until creamy; keep a gentle bubble for about 8–12 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Fold in spinach and black pepper; 1–2 minutes is enough for the greens to soften while keeping their color.
Finish with sliced spring onion.
Taste and adjust the table salt, then serve immediately while the texture is loose, glossy, and hot.

title: Coconut Carrot Savory Oats
tagline: Carrot, coconut milk, curry, and oats make a softly spiced breakfast-for-dinner.
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Toast chopped groundnuts and set aside; stir for 2–3 minutes, stopping as soon as it smells nutty and looks lightly golden.
Soften grated carrot in coconut oil and add curry powder; cook over medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until translucent rather than dark brown.
Stir in oats, coconut milk, and water and simmer until creamy; keep a gentle bubble for about 8–12 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Finish with spring onion and the toasted groundnuts.
Taste and adjust the table salt, then serve immediately while the texture is loose, glossy, and hot.

title: Sweet-Potato Cinnamon Oats
tagline: Mashed sweet potato makes oats creamy, with cinnamon, honey, and toasted sesame.
photo_search_query: sweet potato cinnamon oatmeal bowl food
steps: Wash and dry the produce, complete all chopping, and measure the spices and sauces before turning on the heat.
Boil sweet-potato cubes until soft, drain, and mash; check after 10–12 minutes and drain as soon as a knife slides in with slight resistance.
Simmer oats with oat milk and cinnamon until creamy; keep a gentle bubble for about 15–20 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Stir in the sweet potato and honey.
Toast sesame briefly in a dry pan and scatter it on top; stir for 2–3 minutes, stopping as soon as it smells nutty and looks lightly golden.
Taste and adjust the table salt, then serve immediately while the texture is loose, glossy, and hot.

title: Chicken Drumstick Cabbage Soup
tagline: Drumsticks, cabbage, carrots, and potatoes make a thrifty, restorative pot.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, cut it as directed in the method, and complete all vegetable chopping and seasoning measurements before heating the pan.
Cover drumsticks with water and simmer for 20 minutes, skimming if needed.
Add leeks, garlic, potato, carrot, and black pepper.
When the roots are nearly tender, add shredded cabbage.
Simmer until the chicken is cooked and the vegetables are soft; keep a gentle bubble for about 20–30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Taste the broth and adjust the table salt before serving.

title: Chicken-Mince Ndengu Pot
tagline: Chicken mince stretches through green grams in a thick, spiced tomato gravy.
photo_search_query: chicken mince green gram stew food
steps: Simmer soaked green grams until tender and drain; keep a gentle bubble for about 30–40 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Brown chicken mince in oil; allow 5–7 minutes over medium-high heat, turning only after a deep golden crust forms.
Add onion and garlic-ginger mix.
Add garam masala and tomatoes and reduce to a thick sauce.
Fold in green grams, simmer for 8 minutes.
Finish with parsley.

title: Whole Chicken Coconut Stew
tagline: Bone-in chicken pieces simmer in coconut, tomato, ginger, and warming spices.
steps: Pat the chicken dry, cut it as directed in the method, and complete all vegetable chopping and seasoning measurements before heating the pan.
Brown the chicken pieces in oil in batches; allow 5–7 minutes over medium-high heat, turning only after a deep golden crust forms.
Cook onion, pepper, garlic-ginger mix, curry powder, and tomatoes into a rich base; use medium heat for 4–5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent.
Return chicken, add coconut milk, cover, and simmer gently; keep a gentle bubble for about 20–30 minutes, stirring every few minutes and using the stated doneness cue as the final check.
Cook until every piece is tender and the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Taste and adjust the table salt, rest the finished dish off the heat for 2 minutes, and serve while hot.

title: Kenyan-Spiced Chicken Chapati Flatbreads
tagline: Soft skillet flatbreads wrap garam-masala chicken mince and tomato relish.
steps: Mix chapati flour with yogurt, a pinch of salt, and enough water for a soft dough.
Rest for 10 minutes.
Brown chicken mince with half the onion, garlic-ginger mix, and garam masala; allow 5–7 minutes over medium-high heat, turning only after a deep golden crust forms.
Roll four thin flatbreads and cook each in a lightly oiled skillet until spotted on both sides.
Fill with chicken, diced tomato, remaining onion, and parsley.
Fold and serve.
